content:
As the Republican Party continues to lick its wounds after a shellacking in the midterm elections this month, two of President Donald Trump’s longest-serving advisers have seemingly put an end to their yearslong rivalry ― at least for now.

On Sunday, The Wall Street Journal published an exposé that zoomed in on the “unlikely alliance” between the White House’s newly appointed chief of staff, Stephen Miller, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The two men have become so close during Trump’s second presidential term that Miller’s wife, Katie Miller, described them to the outlet as “besties.”

“It’s certainly not something a lot of people would have predicted,” Rubio said. “If you live long enough, interesting things happen.”

“Our wives joke about you’ve got to be careful not to let Marco and Stephen be together too much because they’re going to come up with some wild idea,” added Miller. “We motivate each other.”

A political attack dog who has been an adviser to the president since his first term, Miller was a driving force behind the Trump administration’s aggressive immigration and deportation policies as well as its efforts to crack down on what Trump and his allies have described as left-wing political extremism.

Miller’s appointment as White House chief of staff earlier this month has been widely interpreted as part of Trump’s plan to “double down” on his hardline MAGA agenda rather than make concessions to Democrats, who will now control both chambers of Congress following their party’s victories in this month’s midterm elections.

Rubio, who arrived in Washington, D.C., in 2011 as a GOP senator from Florida, currently serves as both secretary of state and national security adviser. He is seen as a leading contender to succeed Trump in the 2028 presidential race, especially as political experts suggest the midterm results may impact Vice President JD Vance’s decision to run.

Those familiar with Miller and Rubio’s history will undoubtedly view their recent friendship as a political calculation. A series of leaked emails that surfaced in 2019 found Miller had worked in tandem with far-right publication Breitbart to smear Rubio ahead of the 2016 presidential election.

Miller ― who was an aide to then-Sen. Jeff Sessions (R-Ala.) at the time ― described Rubio in one of the emails as a “pathological” liar. In a separate exchange, he lamented that everyone was “afraid to attack Rubio. Everyone.”

As The Wall Street Journal points out, however, there have been signs of easing tensions between Miller and Rubio for some time. After Trump left office in 2021, Rubio stayed in regular touch with Miller, and sought his advice on speeches.

And in 2023, Miller hosted an event to promote Rubio’s book, “Decades of Decadence: How Our Spoiled Elites Blew America’s Inheritance of Liberty, Security, and Prosperity.” In his introduction, he reportedly left some aides stunned when he described Rubio as “my good friend, principled conservative leader, beloved senator from Florida.”
